about: Settings for the whole proxy. Listeners may override some of them.

keys.meaning: Seconds to receive the whole ClientHello; a slow trickle can't extend it.
Seconds to resolve and connect to the target.
Close after N seconds with no traffic either way. 0 = never.
After one side closes, the other side gets N seconds. 0 = unlimited.
Open connections at most; more are rejected.
Connections from one source (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) still sending their ClientHello. 0 = unlimited.
A list of addresses or networks that may send a PROXY protocol header (v1 or v2). (Called proxy_protocol_from before v1.5.0.)
Bytes moved per step in each direction: the splice pipe size, or the size of each pooled buffer. Clamped to 4096..131072.
Free buffers kept for reuse.
Linux: relay passed-through connections with splice(2), without copying them through the proxy.

Remember a hash of every ClientHello passed through for 10 seconds (at most 1M, newest win) and refuse one that comes in again: it is this proxy's own connection come back (a name or ${host} target that points at this machine), which would otherwise loop until max_connections. Terminated connections are not covered.

Also listen on port 80 (every address the listeners use) and answer each plain HTTP request with a redirect to the same URL on https://: 301 for GET and HEAD, 308 for other methods. Every name is redirected; the HTTPS listeners' rules decide from there. The listener is named http-to-https-redirect (a reserved name); the console can stop and start it.
Pause N microseconds after a short read so data batches up. 0 = off.
Cached allowed name → target decisions. 0 = off.
Cached denied names, kept apart from the allowed ones. 0 = off.
Check the file every N seconds and apply changes (minimum 5). 0 = only on console saves.
Log a one-line summary every N seconds. 0 = never.
Where automatic certificates and the ACME account key are stored.
Where your own CAs live, one folder each (ca001, ca002, ...), with the certificates they issued: see cert: local-ca.
Renew this many days before expiry (or at a third of the lifetime left, if later).
Must be true for cert: auto: you accept the CA's terms of service.
Contact address for the ACME account.
ACME directory URL.
Extra root CA for the ACME server's own HTTPS (a private CA, Pebble).
A list: cert: auto only asks the CA when the name resolves to one of these addresses.

keys.default: required with cert: auto and public_ip_address
keys.meaning: A list of public DNS servers for that check, IP or IP:port: three attempts, each the next server in turn, 3 s each; no answer means no certificate is requested. E.g. [1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 2606:4700:4700::1111].
Legacy: accepted and ignored.
Legacy: accepted and ignored.

about: A list of ports, each with its own rules; at least one is required. Overrides apply to that listener only. With the web console on, its listener (https on 443, console_http otherwise) may be listed by name with options only: no bind or port.

keys.meaning: Up to 64 letters, digits, spaces and -_@#~()[]<>"'; unique ignoring case. What listener: in routes refers to.
Listen addresses, a list: 0.0.0.0 all IPv4, :: all IPv6 and IPv4. The web console's exact bind and port are reserved.
Listen port. Two listeners can't share a port on the same or a wildcard address.
Overrides global for this listener.
A cap for this listener, on top of the global one.
Overrides global for this listener.
Overrides global for this listener.
Overrides global for this listener.
Shared by every connection on this listener, each direction, on top of each rule's limits. E.g. 1Gbit, 100MB/s, 64MiB/s.
For each connection on this listener, each direction.

about: A list of items, each the rules of one listener.

keys.meaning: The listener its rules belong to: a name from listeners, or the console's https / console_http.
Its list of rules (see rules).

about: Each item of a routes item's rules. The most specific domain wins: $no_sni and literal names, then wildcards (more fixed characters first), then $anything_else. A name no rule matches is denied.

keys.meaning: A host name with * wildcards (a * never crosses a dot; as a whole label it is exactly one label), $no_sni for clients that send no name, or $anything_else for every name no other rule takes (checked last).
allow or deny. deny answers with a TLS access_denied alert.
host:port to connect to; an IPv6 host in brackets, [2001:db8::1]:443. ${1}, ${2}, ... are what each * matched; ${host} (or ${0}) is the whole name. Always in braces.
Terminate TLS here: auto (ACME, TLS-ALPN-01); or local-ca / local-ca:ca002 (your own CA in ca_root, made on the CAs page, issuing one certificate per name on first use).

A list. cert: auto: exact names to issue. cert: local-ca: names or globs (*.dev.example.com, several) that get a certificate; any other name is refused (default: every name the rule matches). With $no_sni or $anything_else it may list IP addresses: a client without a host name gets one certificate for all of them (and a $no_sni rule's names), otherwise one for the address it connected to; an IP address a client sends as SNI must be listed.
cert: auto: a script that decides per name not in cert_domains; exit 0 = issue.
The script's arguments, a list of strings with ${1}, ${host} ... filled in.
Terminated rules: speak TLS to the target; false = plaintext.
Verify the target's certificate.
SNI sent to the target and checked in its certificate.
v1 or v2: send the target a PROXY protocol header with the client's address.
Shared by every connection of this rule, each direction. E.g. 1Gbit, 100MB/s, 64MiB/s.
For each connection of this rule, each direction.
A list of entries: the rule answers HTTP itself instead of connecting to a target (needs cert; no target, upstream_* or proxy). The longest prefix wins; none = 404. See serve entries.

about: Each item of a rule's serve list. The client's address goes upstream as X-Forwarded-For; what it sent is replaced.

keys.meaning: reverse_proxy or static_content.
The request path it takes, starting with /. For /api/, a request for /api is redirected to /api/.
http://host:port or https://host:port, no path.
reverse_proxy: /api/x is sent as /x.
reverse_proxy: the Host header sent on.
reverse_proxy to https://: check the target's certificate.
The folder the prefix stands for: /assets/a.css is base_dir/a.css. No listings, no hidden files but .well-known, no symlinks out.
The name of a basic_auth item whose users may use it.

about: A list of user groups that serve entries can ask for (basic_auth: <name>). A password a browser sends is checked once and remembered for 5 minutes.

keys.meaning: What basic_auth: in a serve entry names; unique.
A list of {username, password_hash} (argon2id, or pbkdf2-sha256; make one with tlsproxy --hash-password) or {username, password_plain}.

about: Where the two log streams go: activity (stdout) and problems (stderr).

keys.meaning: File for activity: accepted, route, connected, closed, stats, reloads.
File for problems.
Rotate a file once it reaches this size (K, M, G).
Rotated generations kept: file.1 (newest) .. file.N.
Generations above this number are gzip-compressed.

about: The web console is not in this file: it is set at start-up, so nothing saved from it can change it. On by default; -noconsole turns it off.

keys.meaning: The name it is served under, as a rule of its listener that this file can't override.
Its password, hashed at start-up, or a hash from tlsproxy --hash-password.
Where it listens.
Its port: listener https on 443, console_http on any other. That listener's name, bind and port are reserved.
auto (needs acme_agree_tos: true) or local-ca / local-ca:ca002.
